title: Runway & Dependency Conductor for Multi-Surface Launches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a lightweight 'Conductor' playbook and schedule artifact that coordinates cross-surface launches (runtime, console, API) by mapping critical dependencies, assigned owners, and timeboxed runway slices. This ticket delivers the orchestration artifact used by PM/Eng/Design to: 1) visualize upstream/downstream dependencies, 2) lock integration gates, 3) assign capacity hedges, and 4) publish a cutover calendar with rollback triggers.

Scope: - Produce a standardized runway CSV + interactive timeline (owners, freeze dates, test windows, blackout windows).
- Define gating criteria for each lane (runtime, console, API) and a 3-tier fallback ladder (model-variant fallback, regional shift, capacity reserve).
- Create an automated dependency-check checklist (links to PRs, infra provisioning tickets, migration scripts).
- Run one alignment workshop and one dry-run rehearsal in staging shadow.

Out of scope: Detailed implementation work for individual ENG tickets, deep incident remediation playbooks (these will reference the conductor).

Success metrics: - 95% of critical dependencies validated at the freeze date.
- <1 rollback across all lanes during the first 72 hours of launch.
- No increase in 99th-percentile tail latency beyond 15% relative to baseline during canary windows.

Milestones and timeline: - 2026-03-08: Draft runway & dependency map (owner: Marcus Lee).
- 2026-03-15: Alignment workshop with Eng, Console, SRE, and Design.
- 2026-03-22: Dependency freeze (cut-off for non-blocking changes).
- 2026-03-29 to 2026-04-02: Staging shadow/dry-run including traffic replay and observability checks.
- 2026-04-05 to 2026-04-07: Canary wave 1 (10% traffic), monitor for 48h.
- 2026-04-09 to 2026-04-11: Canary wave 2 (50% traffic).
- 2026-04-12: Full rollout target date (release backstop: 2026-04-14).

Owners & stakeholders: - PM lead: Aisha Patel
- Release conductor: Marcus Lee (Eng PM)
- Runtime engineering lead: Priya Nair
- Console product lead: Ben Huang
- SRE/Observability: Lina Gomez
- Design owner: Omar Williams

Instrumentation & dashboards: - Publish a consolidated launch dashboard with token-level cost delta, request latency p99/p95, error-rate, and rollout percentage by region. Link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/launch-runway

Decision points: - If p99 latency increases >15% in canary wave, pause rollout and escalate to runtime on-call.
- If dependency validation <95% at freeze, shift canary start by +3 days and trigger additional integration work.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: Last-minute infra PRs introduce compatibility issues. Mitigation: Enforce freeze + require compatibility sign-off from runtime lead; add a 24h pre-cutoff merge window with SRE smoke tests.
- Risk: Capacity shortfall during regional traffic surge. Mitigation: Pre-allocate a 20% burst pool in Dedicated and enable autoscale runway for first 48h.

Acceptance criteria: - Runway CSV and interactive timeline published to Drive and linked in this ticket.
- All dependencies have owners and either an OK (merged/provisioned) or an open remediation plan with owner and ETA.
- Alignment workshop recorded and notes posted.
- Staging shadow executed with checklist signed off by SRE and runtime lead.

Artifacts & links: - Runway artifact (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RunwayArtifactExample
- Alignment workshop notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example.com/display/LAUNCH/Runway+Conductor
- Example infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1221
- Observability prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/launch-runway
